item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $71,200 After a Fresh Session Low as the 10-Year Yield Holds Above 5%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $71,200 After a Fresh Session Low as the 10-Year Yield Holds Above 5% Bitcoin price traded near $71,200 on Thursday evening, after slipping to a fresh session low near $71,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. U.S. stocks closed modestly lower and the 10-year Treasury yield held above 5% after Nvidia said CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. The decline started in the morning. Bitcoin price fell below $72,000 before the opening bell and dropped to about $71,150 shortly after 10 a.m. Eastern. A bounce later faded, and the bitcoin price printed a new session low near $71,000 around 6:23 p.m., its weakest level since Aug. 20. It now stands roughly $30,400 below where it closed one year ago. Stocks close lower as yields keep pressure on the bitcoin price The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.39% to 25,366.09, the S&P 500 lost 0.35% to 7,592.40 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.36% to 52,297.09, Reuters reported. Nvidia shares finished 4.3% lower at $166.19, off the day’s lows, after the company said Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and a board member, effective immediately, and named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO. Bitcoin-linked stocks had a harder session. Strategy (MSTR), which MSCI is removing from its USA Index at the Nov. 30 close, finished at $114.41, down 6.5%. Shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), which had bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows through Wednesday, closed at $40.36, down 4.5%. The bond market did much of the afternoon work. The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 12 basis points to 5.105% and reached 5.12%, its highest since Oct. 21, after President Donald Trump said the United States does not need a deal with Iran, Reuters reported. The two-year yield, which tracks Federal Reserve expectations most closely, climbed about 14 basis points to 4.867%. Brent crude settled at $95.82 a barrel, up 3.3%, after attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure escalated. Fed hike bets, a $404 billion deficit and a busy evening of crypto news Higher yields reflect a market that still expects the Fed to tighten again next month. Fed funds futures are pricing in 29 basis points of hikes in December, a quarter-point move as the base case with only slim odds of a half-point step, Reuters reported. Rising rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and that has weighed on the bitcoin price all week. The Treasury added a fiscal reminder after the close. The government ran a $404 billion deficit in October, the first month of fiscal 2027, the Treasury Department said , up 42% from $284 billion a year earlier, as receipts fell to $369 billion and outlays rose to $773 billion. Some benefit payments that would normally have been made on Nov. 1, a Sunday, were shifted into October. The evening also brought a cluster of crypto headlines. item.title: Yaxel Lendeborg Gets a Bay Area Education Over BBQ on NBAT2's 'Rookie Dinner'
item.description: Nov 1, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) gestures after making a three-point basket against the LA Clippers during the fourth quarter at Chase Center. Every NBA rookie learns about the rookie dinner sooner or later, usually when the veterans order half the menu and slide the check across the table at the end of the night. NBA Take-Two Media (NBAT2) and 4.4.Forty Media built a new original series around that tradition, and Rookie Dinner skips the inflated bill in favor of an actual conversation between players from different generations. Each episode puts an NBA rookie at a table in his new city with an established veteran and a local legend, and the meal turns into a crash course on the city he now plays for. NBAT2 started in the Bay Area, and it's hard to think of a better rookie to open with than the one the Warriors have leaned on through the first three weeks of the season. Golden State forward Yaxel Lendeborg sits down at Everett & Jones, the longtime Berkeley barbecue spot, with Denver Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon, 14-year NBA veteran Drew Gooden and Oakland rapper Mistah F.A.B. Gordon grew up in San Jose and Gooden is from Oakland, and NBAT2 says both were home to have their Oakland Soldiers jerseys retired when the episode was filmed. Lendeborg's start Lendeborg took a longer route to the NBA than most lottery picks, starting at the junior college level, then playing two seasons at UAB and a final college year at Michigan before the Warriors took him 11th overall in June. He won Summer League MVP in Las Vegas after averaging 14.8 points, 6.8 rebounds and 4.0 assists for a Golden State team that won the title. The regular season has gone even better than the summer did. Through his first 10 games, Lendeborg is averaging 21.2 points, 7.2 rebounds and 4.0 assists, and with Jimmy Butler out until the new year with a knee injury, he has become the second scoring option next to Stephen Curry. The Clippers learned that the hard way on Nov. 1, when Lendeborg scored a career-high 37 points in a 124-112 Warriors win in a game Golden State played without Curry or Draymond Green. Nov 1, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) gestures after making a three-point basket against the LA Clippers during the fourth quarter at Chase Center. Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Nov 1, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) gestures after making a three-point basket against the LA Clippers during the fourth quarter at Chase Center. The advice The best parts of the episode come when the veterans talk about the things nobody warns young players about. Gordon was honest about how NBA money pushes young players toward materialism, where people pay attention to what car a player drives and who he's seen with, and fitting in can feel more important than it should. item.title: 'A lie' & 'nonsense' - Palmer committed to England, says Rogers
item.description: Cole Palmer and Morgan are Chelsea team-mates [Getty Images] Morgan Rogers says any suggestion Cole Palmer is not committed to England "is a lie" and "nonsense". Rogers scored the opener in Wednesday's 2-1 Uefa Nations League win over Croatia , with Harry Kane adding a penalty on his record-breaking 126th appearance for the men's side. But his Chelsea team-mate, and childhood friend, Palmer had been left out of the squad after boss Thomas Tuchel said he "misses too many chances to impress". The 24-year-old Palmer, who was also not called up for the World Cup, withdrew from the previous England camp in September citing a minor injury. Forward Rogers, also 24, was asked about the criticism of Palmer following the win at Wembley, and told BBC Radio 5 Live: "He wants to be here. "He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. "He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. "But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 or 15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it. "It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. It's a lie. "You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it." Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel? A must pick or unreliable? Tuchel's Palmer dilemma History for Kane but what would England do without him? Struggles under Tuchel In the three years since his England debut, Palmer has only won 14 caps, scoring two goals - including one in the Euro 2024 final defeat by Spain - and having one assist. That is despite scoring 50 Premier League goals with 24 assists. He was named England's men's player of the year for the 2023-24 season after some impressive form, including his strike against Spain in the Berlin showpiece. But Palmer has only featured in three of Tuchel's 27 games since he succeeded Gareth Southgate as manager. Some sketchy form last season, though, meant the former Manchester City player missed out on the the summer World Cup, with England going on to finish third after losing to Argentina in the semi-final. He was named in Tuchel's first squad after that, but withdrew despite having played in all Chelsea's league games to that point. Tuchel said this week: "We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together. "I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. "We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. item.title: Where does Kane rank among all-time England greats?
item.description: [BBC] Harry Kane is now England's most-capped men's player as well as his country's record goalscorer, but harder to quantify is where these achievements place him among the Three Lions' greatest ever players. This is a tricky debate with so many variables and a timescale as old as the game itself and, to my mind, not merely a determination of a player's individual ability but also a measure of their impact upon the nation's psyche. Ballon d'Or winners Stanley Matthews, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen would surely have a shout if the criteria was such, not to mention genius technicians such as Glenn Hoddle, Chris Waddle and John Barnes. Likewise, if any England boss managed to extract the best from Paul Scholes, Steven Gerrard and Frank Lampard they would be surely making a classic late dart from midfield. But to qualify as one of the greatest England players of all time, you need the above ability combined with an impactful overall contribution - those memorable moments and an element of longevity - in a Three Lions shirt. It might be controversial then to leave out Geoff Hurst, who produced the most recognisable performance in England history, while the man he replaced, Jimmy Greaves, would be a shoo-in were it not for injury earlier in the tournament. It is also hard to rank the contribution of those whose best football came outside of major tournaments and before the dawn of continental competitions - see Eddie Hapgood, Tom Finney, Nat Lofthouse, Dixie Dean et al. There are only 10 spots, after all, so here we go. 10. David Beckham Spice Boy. Celebrity. Galactico. There is no argument David Beckham is one of the most iconic England players of all time, but he backed it up on the pitch, too. Beckham was the face of the Three Lions for a generation, and to his credit managed to overcome the vicious fallout of his red card against Argentina in 1998. At times he seemed to single-handedly carry England, most notably scoring a 93rd-minute free-kick against Greece to qualify for the 2002 World Cup. Beckham's former team-mate Gary Neville called him the "most influential player out of England in transforming football". It's true. On top of 115 caps, Beckham was part of Manchester United's 1999 Treble-winning outfit - finishing Ballon d'Or runner-up - before joining Real Madrid. His profile was truly global with spells at LA Galaxy, AC Milan and Paris St-Germain. David Beckham scored 17 goals for England, including five free-kicks [Getty Images] 9. Paul Gascoigne There's arguably no England star fans forged an emotional attachment with more than Gazza - crying with him in 1990, rejoicing in his spectacular effort against Scotland and desperately willing him to connect during that Euro 96 semi-final defeat by Germany. Gascoigne won 57 caps and scored 10 goals. item.title: Husky Stadium is getting a new name and sponsor from Columbia Bank
item.description: A view from above of Husky Stadium at the University of Washington in Seattle. The University of Washington (UW) and Columbia Bank are signing a naming-rights deal to rename Husky Stadium to Columbia Bank Stadium. The deal, penned by UW president Robert Jones and Columbia Bank President Chris Merrywell, is the most expensive naming rights agreement in college football history. Columbia Bank is spending $70 million over the next 10 years for the naming rights to the “Greatest Setting in College Football.” The deal is pending approval from the Board of Regents. If approved, UW Athletics will be making more than $100 million for the department in naming rights alone. Jones said at the press conference that it was “critically important to have a company with deep roots in the community, and highly visible in the state of Washington” to help build and advance the strategic goals of the University of Washington. This comes after Alaska Airlines did not extend its deal for Husky Stadium earlier this year.

item.title: Padres’ Mason Miller ‘delusional’ about accomplishing Jacob Misiorowski-like flame-throwing feat
item.description: Credit: David Frerker-Imagn Images Padres’ Mason Miller ‘delusional’ about accomplishing Jacob Misiorowski-like flame-throwing feat appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mason Miller has established himself as one of the most dominant relievers in baseball, but don’t expect the San Diego Padres flamethrower to start chasing the kind of success Jacob Misiorowski enjoyed as a starting pitcher. Miller was asked on Foul Territory about the possibility of becoming a starter and gave a humorous response while discussing the Milwaukee Brewers ace. Mason Miller had a front-row seat to fellow fireballer Jacob Misiorowski pumping GAS. Could he see himself throwing 100 MPH for 6+ innings? "Maybe in some delusional land." 😂 pic.twitter.com/LdukJmGRzx — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) November 12, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Maybe in some delusional land, yeah. In some delusional world, I am still starting,” Miller said. The Padres star also had plenty of praise for Misiorowski, who took home the National League Cy Young Award after an incredible 2026 campaign. “I think velocity is exciting. I’ve always said for Miz the most impressive thing is his strike-throwing ability. The stuff is off the charts. His consistency throughout the season,” Miller said. There is plenty of reason for Miller to appreciate what Misiorowski accomplished. Both pitchers can overpower hitters with elite velocity, but Misiorowski proved he could maintain that dominance over a full season as a starter. Miller, meanwhile, just earned NL Reliever of the Year honors after putting together a phenomenal season of his own. Miller finished 2026 with a 1.67 ERA and 129 strikeouts across 70 innings. He also recorded 38 saves, establishing himself as one of the most feared late-inning weapons in the National League. This could be the first of several major awards for the Padres closer. Misiorowski and Miller have become two of the most exciting arms in the sport, but their postseason paths went in very different directions. Milwaukee eliminated San Diego in the NLDS before eventually capturing the World Series title. The Padres were the only team to defeat the Brewers in the postseason until Tampa Bay finally got to them in Game 4 of the World Series. Milwaukee isn’t going anywhere anytime soon, especially with Misiorowski leading its rotation. San Diego, meanwhile, reportedly plans to go all-in this offseason as it looks to close the gap on the National League’s top contenders. Related: MLB rumors: Padres, Mariners, Cubs among teams linked to potential Jarren Duran trade with Red Sox Related: How Padres’ Mason Miller reacted to winning NL Reliever of the Year

item.title: Finntastic! European Hurricanes Have a Night in Win Over Kraken in Game 1 of Global Series
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Carolina Hurricanes opened the two-game NHL Global Series in Helsinki, Finland, with a bang. They took the win 4-1 over the Seattle Kraken – with Canes goals ironically all from Europeans – and even performed just the second ever away Storm Surge. With an early start time of 12:00 PM EST, the game fell on a day most Caniacs are busy in the office. Well, the Microsoft Teams outage may have been beneficial for those hockey fans to catch some plays…but, still, without further ado – here is your recap and clips! The game started off strong for the Hurricanes, who outshot the Kraken 15-6 in those first twenty minutes – and outscored them 2-0. Nikolaj Ehlers was the first one to score in the match, in front of his own friends and family who’d made the trek from Denmark to Finland to see him play. The goal was interestingly challenged for goalie interference, but was unsuccessful, leading to a Hurricanes power play. “It’s always nice when you score a goal,” he said during an intermission interview, “my nephew will be pretty psyched about that.” Nikolaj Ehlers gets the Hurricanes on the board first in Helsinki! …And yes, the Canes' goal song (and power play music) were played It was challenged by the Kraken for goalie interference due to Jackson Blake's position near the crease, but ultimately remained on the board… pic.twitter.com/lQkI05A77q — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) November 12, 2026 It wasn’t but just 1:06 later when Sebastian Aho scored on the man advantage , to the delight of Finnish fans. When the public announcer listed Aho as the goalscorer when play resumed, the crowds in the stands cheered pretty wildly – great stuff. A whole lotta cheers from fans in the stands in Helsinki as the PA announced Sebastian Aho's goal 👀 #CarolinaCulture #SeaKraken #NHL https://t.co/76qt7QXPHx pic.twitter.com/psrmbrnhyQ — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) November 12, 2026 In the second period, there was only one goal scored – but oh such a special one as defenseman Juuso Valimaki found the back of the net . The Tampere native had been put back into the roster, with Alexander Nikishin having been scratched – extending the lead just two hours out from his hometown. …We also had a pretty cool stoppage in play in which they had a groovy version of ‘Country Roads’ over the speakers . We've got a blueliner goal as Juuso Valimaki extends the Hurricanes' lead 3-0 in his home country! 🥹 #CarolinaCulture #SeaKraken #NHL pic.twitter.com/0wxPIWHwBx — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) November 12, 2026 As for the third period, the fourth goal was scored by Aho to make it four-to-nothing, but Frederick Gaudreau managed to get one back . item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. Michigan State Spartans defensive back Charles Brantley (4) tackles Illinois Fighting Illini wide receiver Collin Dixon (17) in a Big 10 football game at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Isaac Ritchey | iritchey@mlive

item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. Without Moore, Oregon scored 42 points over three games and lost twice while rotating between backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Moore was injured on Sept. 26 at USC while sliding to end a 10-yard run to the USC 13-yard line. As Moore began to slide, Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II hit him in the head with his shoulder. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, center bottom, takes a hard tackle by lSouthern California inebacker Desman Stephens II, center top, during the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill) AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Moore was taken off the field in a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Following Moore’s injury, Raiola entered the game and led the Ducks to a 41-27 win. Moore entered the concussion protocol but returned to practice the following bye week. Speculation was that Moore would return once he cleared the protocols. But each subsequent availability report listed Moore as out. On Oct. 10, Oregon lost 17-15 to UCLA, with Raiola struggling through three quarters before being replaced in the fourth quarter by Thomas. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.title: Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous
item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

item.title: Dodgers GM Brandon Gomes Gives Update on Kiké Hernández’s Free Agency
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes addressed the free-agent status of longtime veteran Kiké Hernández. Where the Dodgers stand with Kike Hernandez Hernandez is once again a free agen t after a season with the Dodgers, though this time his return does not seem as imminent as before. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) During the MLB General Managers’ meetings, Gomes was asked about the pending free agent as the days count down until the lockout. “I think Kiké’s been such a huge part of what we’ve done in the past and we’ll continue to have those conversations, but what that looks like right now, I don’t know,” Gomes said of Hernandez. Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Enrique Hernandez (8) reacts after losing the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs to the Milwaukee Brewers at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Seemingly, as Hernandez and the Dodgers try to assess his market and weigh possible upgrades, there is still an open line of communication, which opens a path for a reunion down the line. However, factors may lead the team to bring in some fresh blood to the batting order. Why the Dodgers may not bring back Hernandez Last year, the Dodgers and Hernandez did a bit of song and dance before he re-signed ahead of Spring Training. Despite recovering from elbow surgery, he agreed to a one-year, $5 million contract and started the season on the injured list until May, when he came back, just to once again get hurt, this time with an abdominal tear. He missed another handful of months before coming back for the end of the season and the postseason. Over the regular season, he hit .222/.271/.400 in 41 games, with four home runs, 12 RBIs, 28 strikeouts, and just six walks. Oct 14, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Enrique Hernandez (8) reacts to striking out against the Milwaukee Brewers during the sixth inning in game three of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The postseason, aside from a big home run in the NLDS, was no different: 1-for-14 with no walks and three strikeouts. With elbow injuries impacting him over the last two years, along with the abdominal injury, Hernandez’s injury record has become somewhat alarming, and at age 35, is it possible for things to get better? The Dodgers felt like an old squad that could use some new blood, and if they want to pave the way for younger position players, letting Hernandez go could be a reasonable move.

item.title: Steelers center Zach Frazier tabbed as midseason First-Team All-Pro
item.description: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers offensive line has been the most pleasant surprise of the season so far. Pittsburgh has one of the best rushing attacks in the entire league through nine weeks, averaging 117.9 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s offensive line is finally turning the corner and emerging as a serious strength of the team, and it all starts with their center, Zach Frazier. ESPN’s Bill Barnwell put together his midseason All-Pro team , with the Steelers center earning first-team honors. Frazier’s 79.5 overall PFF grade is first among centers this season. The center has posted his best grades as a run and pass blocker of his career this season. New column: My midseason awards + All-Pro team https://t.co/TywmDBPYUr pic.twitter.com/U1ckcuHeFm — Bill Barnwell (@billbarnwell) November 12, 2026 As well as being named to Barnwell’s midseason All-Pro team, Frazier was also named a top contender for the Protector of the Year award. “With Creed Humphrey’s problems snapping the football becoming more conspicuous, Frazier has emerged for me as the best center in football,” Barnwell said. “The Steelers have quietly fielded one of the league’s most efficient run games this season, and so much of that is what Frazier is able to do as the pivot. Watch here, as he reaches and manhandles Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger to spring Jaylen Warren for a 24-yard gain. Frazier has also given up only one sack and four quick pressures all season, per NFL Next Gen Stats.” There is no denying that Frazier is putting together the best season of his career. The 51st overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft is due for an extension this summer that will almost certainly make him one of, if not the highest-paid center in the league. Frazier will continue to be one of the Steelers’ key building blocks for years to come, and he’s finally getting the attention he deserves. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! item.title: USC Volleyball Hosts Oregon, Washington to End Home Slate
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google USC women’s volleyball (10-14, 4-10 Big Ten) wraps up its home schedule at Galen Center this week, hosting No. 12 Oregon on Thursday, Nov. 12, and No. 18 Washington on Saturday, Nov. 14, when the Trojans will honor three players on Senior Day. USC Volleyball Faces Two Ranked Opponents at Galen Center The Trojans’ final two home matches of 2026 both come against ranked former Pac-12 rivals. Oregon arrives at 20-4 overall and 11-3 in the Big Ten for a 6 p.m. PT first serve on Thursday, streamed on B1G+. Washington, 18-5 overall and 9-5 in conference play, follows on Saturday at 7 p.m. PT on BTN. That match doubles as Senior Day and the home finale. Match Date Time (PT) Opponent Record TV/Stream USC vs. No. 12 Oregon Thursday, Nov. 12 6 p.m. 20-4, 11-3 B1G+ USC vs. No. 18 Washington (Senior Day) Saturday, Nov. 14 7 p.m. 18-5, 9-5 BTN View this post on Instagram A post shared by USC Women's Volleyball (@uscwomensvolley) Senior Day Honors Ford, Wijay and Faumuina Before Saturday’s match against the Huskies, USC will hold pre-match ceremonies to celebrate the careers of Leah Ford, London Wijay and Adonia Faumuina. All three are projected starters this week. Faumuina, a redshirt senior outside hitter from Long Beach, and Wijay, a redshirt junior outside hitter from Porter Ranch, are both Southern California products, while Ford anchors the middle as a redshirt junior. USC outside hitter London Wijay passes the ball as the Oregon Ducks host the USC Trojans on Nov. 19, 2025, at Matthew Knight Arena in Eugene, Oregon. Megan Moenoa Leads Trojans Into Notable Coaching Matchups USC is led by Megan Moenoa, a fourth-year associate head coach who was named the Trojans’ interim head coach on Oct. 5, 2026. Both matches this week carry a coaching storyline. Thursday pairs Moenoa with Oregon head coach Trent Kersten, both UCLA graduates from 2015. Moenoa won the 2011 NCAA title as the Bruins’ setter. Saturday’s meeting with Washington and head coach Leslie Tuiasosopo Gabriel will be the first Big Ten volleyball match to feature two Polynesian women as head coaches. Both are Samoan. Jan 27, 2024; Los Angeles, California, USA; The Southern California Trojans logo at center court at the Galen Center. The Ducks still hold a 6-4 edge over the last 10 matchups. Against Washington, the Trojans lead 49-33 and have won six straight, most recently 3-1 in Seattle on Nov. 9, 2025. Since joining the Big Ten in 2024, USC is 10-2 against the other three former Pac-12 schools, with the losses coming to Oregon in 2024 and UCLA in 2025. Home court has been a challenge this fall. USC is 235-72 all-time at Galen Center but 4-8 there this season, and is 0-6 at home again

item.title: Texas State RB commit Daylon Gordon, a top 2027 Bobcats pledge, flips to Ohio State
item.description: Wylie's Daylon Gordon (1) carries the ball against Wylie East during the second half of a high school football game at Wylie ISD Stadium in Wylie, Friday, Oct. 9, 2026. (Chitose Suzuki/The Dallas Morning News) It's not too often a loss on the recruiting trail can show the strength of a team's scouting prowess, but that might be the case for Texas State football. Daylon Gordon, a running back who pledged to the Bobcats in the spring, has reportedly flipped his commitment to Ohio State. The 5-foot-9 senior out of Wylie was a three-star recruit at the time but has risen up the 247Sports rankings. He's now a four-star prospect overall and according to the site's composite. He was the 33rd-ranked back in the nation but has risen to No. 22. Last season, Gordon rushed 169 times for 1,063 yards and 14 TDs, per 247Sports. He also added 38 receptions for 565 yards and four TDs on a sturdy 14.9 yards per catch. Gabe Brooks, a scouting analyst for 247, wrote in May that Gordon is a "dynamic playmaker" as both a pass catcher and ball carrier. "Natural build for the position with a low center of gravity and broad-shouldered stature," he wrote. "Solid track and field data accompanies equally respectable testing numbers." Brooks also praised his top-end speed and acceleration. So it's no surprise the Buckeyes would be interested. He also held offers from Texas Tech, Utah, Florida State, Ole Miss and others. Texas State head coach GJ Kinne still has one potential back committed in the class: Isaiah Reed, who is listed by some recruiting outlets as an ATH, out of Hamshire. But Alabama recently extended him an offer. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Start your day with the must-read headlines from Austin's most trusted news source. item.title: How UTSA plans to show resilience in critical clash with North Texas
item.description: UTSA Roadrunners running back Will Henderson III (1) celebrates after rushing for a touchdown during the second quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) Finding a team that was still carrying the embarrassment of last week's blowout loss to Florida Atlantic as UTSA stepped onto the practice field Tuesday, coach Jeff Traylor turned to the Bible verse Philippians 3:13-14. "Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead, I press on toward the goal," the verse reads. Traylor said real coaching starts in the face of adversity, and the Roadrunners met plenty in a 60-29 loss at FAU last Thursday that ended UTSA's unbeaten run through the American Conference. In his seventh year leading the program, Traylor knows longtime observers and even some of the players have likely grown tired of hearing his familiar mantras, but he has no plans on breaking from the core beliefs that helped set the foundation of the program. The approach has helped the Roadrunners consistently rebound from setbacks under Traylor, and as UTSA prepares to host North Texas at 8 p.m. Saturday in the Alamodome with conference title hopes still in the balance, receiver Mekhi Anderson said the team's confidence has never wavered. "It's just fighting for your brothers, knowing just that you have guys that's with you through everything," Anderson said. "Through any challenging moments or any adversity, we just keep fighting. We don't give up. You will never see us go away." READ MORE: How UTSA's defense aims to find consistency in matchup against North Texas The Roadrunners are 17-6 following a loss since Traylor took over prior to the 2020 season, including a 15-4 mark since 2021. UTSA has dropped back-to-back matchups against Group of Six competition only three times since Traylor took the helm, and never in consecutive weeks. Anderson, in his third year with the Roadrunners, pointed to the "Ubuntu" mindset the team has used as a rallying cry this season, drawing on the old African phrase that means "I am because we are." Offensive lineman Luke Lapeze, who stands as the longest tenured Roadrunner after joining the team in 2021, said that idea was central to UTSA's culture long before they gave it a name. "It's just grit," Lapeze said. "Coach Traylor does a great job and really believes in us and treats us really, really well. So we want to do right by him, and play well for him and the staff. ... It's been a motto this year, but in years past, we've kind of always had that, where we play for each other and our coaches." UTSA Roadrunners quarterback Owen McCown (2) scrambles past Rice Owls defensive lineman Aquantis Clemmons (57) during the first quarter in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) After getting "a good serving of humble pie" against FAU, Lapeze said he's seen a team that looks "a lot more locked in" this week. item.title: '100 per cent wrong, utter nonsense': Pat Cummins hits out at Usman Khawaja over Sandpapergate allegations in no-holds-barred press conference
item.description: '100 per cent wrong, utter nonsense': Pat Cummins hits out at Usman Khawaja over Sandpapergate allegations in no-holds-barred press conference originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Australia Test and ODI captain Pat Cummins has finally responded to Usman Khawaja's allegations about Sandpapergate. Cummins has hit out at Khawaja for claiming the bowlers knew about Sandpaper use in Cape Town. Cummins stood by the bowlers' statement from 2021. Cummins finally responds to Khawaja's allegations about Sandpapergate Australia's Test and ODI captain Pat Cummins has finally addressed the controversy that has rocked Australian cricket in the last one week. It all started after former national team opener Usman Khawaja made explosive claims about the infamous 'Sandpapergate' from 2018 during Australia's tour of South Africa. In his recently released autobiography, 'Sabr', Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian team from the 2018 South Africa tour was aware of the use of sandpaper in Cape Town and not just the three players who were implicated. The official line from Cricket Australia since the incident in Cape Town has held that only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft had knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball during the third Test against South Africa. The aim, as understood at the time, was to scuff the surface and help the ball swing in reverse, and the three men were handed bans of up upto 12 months for their roles. However, Khawaja's claims in his book have brought the incident back into the limelight, as the southpaw said every Australian player knew about it, including the bowlers. MORE: 'Raises more questions': Johnson calls out Khawaja for dodging questions on Cummins Pat Cummins hits out at Usman Khawaja over Sandpapergate allegations Days after Khawaja's revelation that rocked, not just Australian cricket, but the entire cricket world, Cummins has finally decided to address the incident in a no-holds-barred press conference. On Friday, Cummins addressed the media to clarify his position in the incident, as he said, "When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, that is 100% wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years, I did not know that was happening." He added, But I think Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that. He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense. I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out that Usman admitted that he told Cam [Bancroft] to be careful when using sandpaper. That's not the Usman that I know. It's not the Usman that I think, or that has been part of a team that's helped rebuild this Australian cricket culture over the last eight years, and you know the Usman that would have stopped that from happening there and then. Usman's a friend, but frien

item.title: Rockets Guard Marcus Smart Hit With Multiple-Game Suspension For Punching Charles Bassey
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images It was a heated scene at the Toyota Center on Wednesday, where the Golden State Warriors and Houston Rockets faced off for the first time this season. With nearly identical records and stars on both sides, we expected a highly competitive matchup , but nobody was prepared for the violence that followed. With both teams battling hard, tensions boiled over late in the third quarter when veteran guard Marcus Smart got tangled up with Warriors big man Charles Bassey . Smart was ejected after connecting on a punch at mid-court, and the league announced further punishment today: a three-game suspension. “The NBA is suspending Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart for three games for punching Golden State center Charles Bassey on Wednesday night,” reported ESPN’s Shams Charania . In physical altercations like this, the NBA often responds with fines or suspensions for those involved. Usually, however, the suspension is limited to one game, allowing for a quick return. In this case, the NBA came down harder, no doubt because Smart actually connected with a punch to the face. MARCUS SMART PUNCHES CHARLES BASSEY 😳 https://t.co/MUsLlDHCz4 — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 12, 2026 It’s unclear what set off the altercation, but Bassey likely had a sense of what was coming. He had been tussling with Smart for a while by that point, and Rockets coach Ime Udoka says he had personally challenged Smart to take physical action. “I didn’t see it, but Marcus started talking to him, and he says they got wrapped up and his elbow that he had hurt got bent up,” said Udoka after the game . “So he said something to him, and Bassey said, ‘What you gonna do?’ and he did it.” Bassey did not receive any punishment from the altercation, but he sure had a lot to say after yesterday’s game. With a smile, he called Smart “fake tough” and “dirty” for getting physical over a purely basketball play. Now, Bassey will move on to the next game, while Marcus has to spend a week on the sidelines. Smart, 32, joined the Rockets this summer after a short stint with the Lakers . Wanting a place where he could play a big role on a contending team, he felt Houston was a good fit, if for nothing else than a chance to reunite with his former coach, Ime Udoka. So far, the results have been impressive. This season, at 9-3, the Rockets are third in the West, just 1.5 games back from the No. 1-seeded Lakers. They are top 10 in both offensive and defensive rating, thanks to a stacked roster that includes Kevin Durant , Alperen Sengun , Amen Thompson , and Fred VanVleet . Smart, meanwhile, has provided steady contributions off the bench. In nine games this season, the 6’3″ guard has averaged 8.3 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 2.0 assists on 43.9% shooting from the field. His defense and playmaking in the backcourt have provided a critical boost for the Rockets, who will now have to play without him for the next three games. The game tomorrow against the Utah J

item.title: Juke Harris still looking to settle in with Tennessee
item.description: Tennessee guard Juke Harris (2) attempts a shot past Radford guard Mathieu Grujicic (9) during a college basketball game between Tennessee and Radford at Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center in Knoxville on Nov. 9, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s early, but the Juke Harris-Tennessee marriage is off to a slow start — that may be putting it mildly. Through two official games, Harris has just 13 total points. The Wake Forest transfer scored seven points in the home opener against Wofford, then just six points against Radford on Monday. Harris is 3-13 from the field and 2-9 from three-point range. This production is a continuation of what we saw during the preseason scrimmages against Xavier and Duke. “I think for Juke this is a new experience,” Tennessee assistant coach Earl Grant said on Thursday. “He played 32 minutes a game last year, averaged 20 points a game. He took the most attempts on his team, played the most minutes. And his team depended on him to be their leading scorer all the time. I think now he’s on a team with a lot of guys who can do a lot of things.” Harris played 35 minutes per game last season for the Demon Deacons, averaging over 21 points per game. He shot 44 percent from the field while handing a near 30 percent usage rate. So far this season, Harris has a 17.7 percent usage rate. That’s a number that’s likely to tick up quickly, but as Grant noted, Tennessee isn’t short on options. Terrence Hill Jr. has proven to be the creator to this point. We’ve also seen Tyler Lundblade and Dai Dai Ames handle the ball and create quite a bit through two games. Troy Henderson has also gotten in on the action. Still, the upside of this team likely travels through Harris, who has proven plenty capable of carrying a roster before. “He’s trying to carve out what he has to do for Tennessee basketball for Tennessee basketball to win,” Grant continued. “And I think scoring is a big part of that, but he’s gotta defend, he’s gotta rebound, he’s gotta lead, he’s gotta talk. And he’s had more people around him that can score, as well, so he may have to facilitate at times.” For Rick Barnes, it’s a moving target. He’s likely going to tinker with his starting lineups and rotations over the next several weeks. However, after Friday’s game against Tennessee State, things begin getting very real. The Volunteers welcome Michigan State — fresh off of a win over Duke this week — to Food City Center on Tuesday. The Players Era Tournament gets going a week after that in Las Vegas. Getting Harris going would certainly be a massive boost heading into that massive event on Thanksgiving week.

item.title: Pochettino set to sign two-and-a-half year deal at Man Utd
item.description: Pochettino set to sign two-and-a-half year deal at Man Utd Mauricio Pochettino is set to sign a two-and-a-half year deal to become Manchester United’s new head coach. United are set to pay the release clause in the Argentine’s contract with the United States, worth around $10million (£7.4m), after identifying him as their preferred choice to replace Michael Carrick. Carrick and his coaching staff were relieved of their duties on Thursday morning following a poor run of results. Pochettino, who has previously managed Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the Premier League, is now set to take over at Old Trafford. He is expected to take charge of the USA during this international break for the final time before joining United. item.title: Dan Hurley loses sharpshooting Duke transfer to foot injury that needs surgery
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images Dan Hurley loses sharpshooting Duke transfer to foot injury that needs surgery appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The UConn Huskies have begun the 2026-27 college basketball season at 3-0, including a big win against the defending champion Michigan Wolverines . But as the Huskies appear to be among the early contenders for the national championship, they’re going to be short-handed in the near future. Sophomore guard Nik Khamenia suffered a foot injury during UConn’s win against Wagner on Monday, and will be sidelined for six to eight weeks, the team announced. Nik Khamenia will undergo surgery for the foot injury, and he’s expected to make a full recovery putting his potential return to UConn’s lineup somewhere around New Year. The Huskies still have a few formidable opponents on their non-conference schedule, but Khamenia’s return could coincide with the beginning of Big East play. Against Wagner, Khamenia played only seven minutes before sustaining the injury late in the first half. He finished with 11 points and one rebound while shooting 4-of-5 from the field and 3-of-3 from the 3-point line. He did not return after exiting the game. After transferring from Duke where he was part of the second unit, the Southern California native had stepped right in to a starting role with the Huskies. item.title: Jane Street Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 54% to 4.1 Million Shares
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Jane Street Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 54% to 4.1 Million Shares Jane Street Group raised its Strategy (MSTR) stake 53.8% in the third quarter, to 4,119,097 shares, a Form 13F filed Thursday shows, a position dated to Sept. 30 that does not capture any trades the firm may have made since then. Those caveats matter as much as the increase. Jane Street is a trading firm, and one of the largest market makers in stocks, ETFs, and options, and the same filing lists call options covering 13,573,000 Strategy shares and put options covering 13,991,800 shares, each more than three times the size of the common stake. Some of that stock is likely a hedge for the options and market-making book rather than a straight bet on the company. The 13F does not say how much. The shares were valued at $630.6 million in the filing, using the Sept. 30 price of $153.09. Strategy has fallen about 25% since then. At Thursday’s close of $114.41, the same 4,119,097 shares were worth about $471 million. The Class A position is up 1,441,475 shares from the 2,677,622 Jane Street reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at $232.8 million. The firm filed about four days ahead of the Nov. 16 deadline; the SEC accepted the report at 4:04 p.m. Eastern on Thursday. Call and put positions that dwarf Strategy’s stock The options lines were already large in the second quarter and grew again. Calls covering 13,573,000 shares were valued at $2.08 billion in the new filing, and puts covering 13,991,800 shares, listed in two rows, were valued at $2.14 billion. Those figures use the same Sept. 30 share price as the common-stock line; a 13F reports the underlying shares the options cover, not the cash premium paid for the contracts. The report is a holdings filing that folds in positions across seven other included managers, among them Jane Street Capital, Jane Street Options and Jane Street Global Trading, so the Strategy lines can include inventory across the group rather than a single proprietary bet. Authorized Signatory Jeremy Kahn signed the report in New York on Nov. 12. The table lists 14,764 entries valued at $1.19 trillion. Other early 13Fs so far, with bigger names still to file Jane Street’s 53.8% increase was the sharpest percentage increase among the large Strategy stakes in Thursday’s early 13F wave. Capital International Investors, a Capital Group unit, raised its stake 4.5% to 36,467,109 shares, worth about $4.17 billion at Thursday’s close. Invesco added 10.9%, to 10,362,698 shares, worth about $1.19 billion. Renaissance Technologies cut its position 41%, to 1,515,560 shares, worth about $173 million, and left the spot bitcoin ETF holdings it had reported at midyear, including BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust. JPMorgan Chase, in a filing already reported , lifted its Strategy stake 36% to 848,932 shares and held 11.4 million IBIT shares, worth about $460 million at Thursday’s close. item.title: Microsoft struggling to fix massive cloud outage that's taken down email and Intune
item.description: Microsoft is struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became “overwhelmed” and its attempts to fix the problem failed. The incident started at around 18:00 UTC on November 12, and meant services including Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot 365, and Defender for Office 365 became unavailable. Admins trying to figure out what was wrong couldn’t access tools like Intune or the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center – they went down, too. On its X feed, Microsoft blamed “a problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable.” The company said it hasn’t spotted any changes to its systems that might have sparked the incident, but its early investigation “indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health.” The company’s status page offers contradictory information, saying Microsoft’s people are “assessing whether reverting the small number of recent configuration updates we identified could help accelerate recovery.” According to a Xeet published at around 22:00 UTC, Microsoft said it found and validated an alternative service health check method, “which allowed a subset of affected servers to successfully return to service.” “We're continuing to work through restarting and validating the affected servers to safely return them to service, and we're exploring opportunities to expedite this process,” the company wrote. But those efforts may not be working. “We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” the status page advises. “Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.” The incident means email is not flowing for many Microsoft customers: friends and family of Reg writers tell us their working days are severely disrupted. Microsoft’s most recent Xeet on the matter, published about an hour before this story went live, says it's trying to validate a potential recovery by “isolating a portion of infrastructure, restarting affected components, and reintroducing traffic to confirm the services remain stable before applying the change more broadly.” But the software giant hasn’t offered any timeline for full service restoration. This is a developing situation and The Reg will update this story as more information becomes available. ®

item.title: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges prostate cancer tests for all men
item.description: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that all men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years. item.title: Italy stun France 3-1 to hand Zidane first defeat as Les Bleus coach
item.description: Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus. France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes. Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi’s pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki. Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini’s side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco’s cut-back. Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara. Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift. Belgium host Italy on Sunday and France are at home to Turkey. Turkey slid to a fifth straight loss as they went down 2-1 to Belgium in Izmir. Arda Guler’s magnificent free-kick put Turkey ahead under new coach and former midfielder Sergen Yalcin, but Belgium struck twice in quick succession with goals from Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere to come away with victory. item.title: DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms. Neither the Justice Department nor Europol split the $234 million between cash and cryptocurrency, and neither named bitcoin or any other coin in the official totals. Europol put the European share at more than €60 million in cash and cryptocurrencies, alongside 950 kilograms of drugs and 57 firearms, and the U.S. share at more than €150 million, or $166 million, in cash and cryptocurrencies, plus more than 4.8 metric tons of drugs and 152 firearms. Those regional money figures still combine cash and crypto. Europol said its forensic and blockchain analysis teams traced illicit transactions as part of the work. Individual cases point to Monero and bitcoin The closest official window into how the vendors were paid comes from the cases the Justice Department highlighted and from court papers posted with the announcement. Alexander Green, 32, of Jacksonville, North Carolina, was arrested in June and charged in the Southern District of Ohio with conspiracy to distribute controlled substances, including fentanyl. The department said he allegedly operated a vendor called STARLABS on DrugHub, which it described as a Monero-only dark web market, and that the group has been linked to two overdose deaths. A criminal complaint says undercover purchases from STARLABS were made “in exchange for cryptocurrency.” If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in prison. In a separate Florida arrest, brothers Stanislav Chernyshov, 30, and Vladislav Chernyshov, 35, are charged in the Eastern District of Virginia with conspiracy to distribute Schedule I synthetic opioids. item.description: The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment. “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10. item.title: Google promises its new smart specs won't give creeps their ideal view
item.description: It’s been nearly a decade since Google ditched its ill-fated "Glass" product, an early attempt at making smart glasses. Now, as rivals like Meta enter the market with arguably more stylish kit, the Chocolate Factory has returned to the market and this time promises it won't invade your privacy. As announced Thursday, Google has decided not to make wearables itself, instead turning Samsung and eyeglass makers Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Like most of the rest of this generation of smart glasses, none of the nine styles available feature heads-up displays, just cameras and audio feedback from Gemini. Google suggests its smart specs give users a chance to ask its Gemini chatbot questions about what they see, or have the AI speak turn-by-turn directions. Wearers of the device can also push a button or speak a command to activate the built-in 12MP camera and shoot snaps or video. Warby Parker's version of the glasses will come in three styles, with prescription and sunglass lenses available. Prices start at $395. The same lens options are available in the six frames from Gentle Monster, which will start at $449. Both manufacturers promise nine hours of battery life, boosted by charging cases that can refresh the glasses up to seven times. Preorders for both are available now, with shipments arriving, and sales beginning, on December 10. Google promises privacy The Chocolate Factory, not exactly known for being reliable with its privacy claims, is insisting that this latest generation of smart glasses won’t produce another generation of “glassholes,” folk whose focus on wearable devices became synonymous with being creepy and rude to those around them. Google has some catchup to do to that end, given Meta’s smart glasses have already landed it in hot water over privacy concerns that have led to some calling the devices “ pervert glasses .” Unsurprisingly, at around the same time it announced its new "intelligent eyeware," Google published a blog post detailing how it intends to mitigate privacy concerns. As with similar headsets, there’s a little light that comes on whenever the camera is activated. In Google’s case, it claims that light is tamper-resistant and designed to disable recording if something as small and simple as a bit of hair blocks a view of the light. It’s not clear how the tamper proofing works from Google’s statements, but a spokesperson told us a combination of hardware and software is used to detect attempts to disable or disrupt privacy features. “We're committed to continuously improving the effectiveness of these solutions as new attack vectors are identified,” Google told us. The glasses don't save images or video captured by the camera into a user’s Gemini history, Google said, nor are visuals used to train the company’s AI models or target advertisements. Google told us it does save audio recordings and transcripts of conversations with Gemini that users create while wearing the glasses but again insists that those aren’t

item.title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
item.description: Key US lawmakers on Thursday called for clarity on what the Trump administration knew about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chip giant announced his departure. Huang, now Nvidia’s former CEO, had pushed for looser rules on sales of US chips to China — crucial in the AI race — and the controversy has reenergized advocates of a hard line on Beijing, days before Donald Trump travels to China. “Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put US national security at risk,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on social media. “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset,” he added. Huang, a co-founder of the AI chip giant, on Sunday acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence suspects her of working for Beijing, which has strongly denied the allegations. ‘Obvious Threat’ According to The New York Times, Trump was informed of the suspicions last year, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said on Monday he knew “the FBI is looking into” the affair, adding that he expected Huang to be “in good shape.” He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy. U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP Huang was ultimately brought down by the scandal on Thursday, when the company’s board announced his departure, effective immediately. Lawmakers are also raising questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to impose restrictions on exports of the chips to China. Three Republican House committee chairmen had already said they wanted to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January after winning the midterm elections, have also said they intend to look more closely into the affair. The top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees told Lutnick in a letter on Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s “scheme to approve and tax” Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms linked to Beijing’s government and military. They accuse Lutnick and Trump of ignoring the “obvious national security threat” posed by the ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence agent, even though they had reportedly been informed of them.
